blocks.text: Correlation handled numeric features against a numeric target, and Chi-Square handled categorical features against a categorical target. One genuine combination remains, a numeric feature evaluated against a categorical target, exactly the classification scenario that dominates a huge share of real machine learning problems. ANOVA, short for Analysis of Variance, is the genuine filter method built specifically for this exact case.

This topic covers how ANOVA directly extends the group means comparison first introduced in Bivariate Analysis into a precise statistical test, the F-statistic itself, comparing variance between groups against variance within them, how to read a high or low F-statistic for feature relevance, the real assumptions this test relies on, and how to apply it directly with scikit-learn, closing out this module entire filter method family.
1. Building Directly on Group Means

blocks.alt: Group means feed directly into ANOVA

blocks.text: ANOVA genuinely starts from the exact same comparison first introduced back in Bivariate Analysis, grouping a numeric feature by a categorical variable and comparing its average value across each group. There, price was genuinely compared across city and suburb location categories using a grouped boxplot, ANOVA turns that genuine same comparison into a precise, quantified statistical test.

This connection is genuinely worth holding onto directly, ANOVA is not introducing an unfamiliar new comparison, it is formalizing a comparison already made visually and intuitively much earlier in this course, into a real number that can rank features automatically.
2. The F-Statistic: Between-Group Versus Within-Group Variance

blocks.alt: Between-group variance and within-group variance together produce the F-statistic

blocks.text: The F-statistic genuinely divides two quantities, the variance between the different group means, how spread out those group averages are from each other, by the variance within each individual group, how spread out the values are inside any one single group. A feature that genuinely distinguishes the target classes well should show group means that differ considerably more than the natural spread inside any one group.

This ratio is genuinely the entire core insight behind ANOVA, it is not enough for group means to simply differ, they need to differ by more than the natural, ordinary variation already present within each group, otherwise that difference could genuinely just be noise.
3. Reading a High F-Statistic

blocks.alt: A high F-statistic points to a real group difference

blocks.text: A genuinely high F-statistic means the group means differ meaningfully more than the natural variation within each group would predict, a genuine, real signal that this feature actually helps distinguish between the target classes. Square footage showing genuinely, considerably different average values across bought versus not bought groups would produce a genuinely high F-statistic.

This is exactly the signal worth acting on directly in feature selection, a genuinely high F-statistic argues strongly for keeping that feature, since it demonstrates a real, measurable relationship to the target classes.
4. Reading a Low F-Statistic

blocks.alt: A low F-statistic points to no real group difference

blocks.text: A genuinely low F-statistic means the group means look similar to each other, once the natural variation within each group is accounted for, suggesting this feature genuinely does not help distinguish the target classes well. A feature like an arbitrary internal ID number would typically produce a genuinely low F-statistic, since it carries no real relationship to the actual target at all.

Features with a genuinely low F-statistic are strong genuine candidates for removal, exactly the same top-k selection logic used throughout this entire filter method family, just powered by a different, appropriate statistical test for this specific variable type combination.

blocks.text: 5. A Worked Example

blocks.alt: Three groups run through an F-test to find a significant difference

blocks.text: Applying scikit-learn SelectKBest with the f_classif scoring function shows ANOVA directly in action, on a small classification dataset.

code.content:
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, f_classif
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 2100, 2400, 950, 1250, 2200, 2450],
    "shoe_size_unrelated": [8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9, 7, 10],
})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1])

selector = SelectKBest(score_func=f_classif, k=1)
selector.fit(X, y)

print("F-statistics:", selector.scores_)
print("Selected:", X.columns[selector.get_support()].tolist())

blocks.text: square_feet, whose values genuinely separate cleanly between the two target classes here, receives a genuinely high F-statistic and gets selected, while shoe_size_unrelated, deliberately overlapping between both classes, genuinely receives a much lower score.

blocks.text: 6. The Real Assumptions Behind ANOVA

blocks.alt: ANOVA assumes normally distributed groups with roughly equal variance

blocks.text: ANOVA genuinely works best when the numeric feature is roughly normally distributed within each target group, directly connecting back to the normality checks covered in Distribution Analysis, and when the spread, or variance, of that feature is genuinely similar across every group being compared.

When these assumptions are genuinely, badly violated, a heavily skewed feature within one group but not another, for instance, the resulting F-statistic can become genuinely less reliable, worth keeping in mind as a real caveat rather than treating ANOVA output as an absolute, unquestionable truth in every case.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: ANOVA reliability genuinely depends on its underlying assumptions holding reasonably well. A feature severely skewed within one group but not another, checked using the tools from Distribution Analysis, deserves a second look before trusting its F-statistic outright.

blocks.text: 7. Completing the Filter Method Family

blocks.alt: Correlation for numeric data, chi-square for categorical data, and ANOVA for numeric versus categorical complete the filter family

blocks.text: Correlation, Chi-Square, and ANOVA together now genuinely cover every meaningful combination of feature and target type, numeric to numeric, categorical to categorical, and numeric to categorical. Any real dataset, whatever mix of feature and target types it actually contains, now has a genuine, appropriate filter method statistical test available.

This completes the entire filter method family this module opened with, fast, statistical, and model independent selection, ready to be applied as a genuinely quick first pass before considering the more expensive, model aware families covered next.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Match the scoring function to the real variable types involved: f_regression for a numeric target, chi2 for a categorical feature and target, and f_classif for a numeric feature against a categorical target.

blocks.text: 8. ANOVA Versus What Comes Next

Filter Methods, Correlation, Chi-Square, and ANOVA together close out the genuinely fast, statistical, model independent family this module opened with. Every technique in that family shares the same real limitation flagged back in Filter Methods, scoring each feature independently, missing genuine interaction effects, and never actually reflecting how a real, specific model would use those features together.

The next topic, Wrapper Methods, opens this module second genuine family, one that trains an actual model repeatedly to directly measure real, practical performance across different feature subsets, considerably more accurate, but genuinely far more computationally expensive than anything covered so far in this module.

items: ANOVA genuinely tests whether a numeric feature mean differs meaningfully across categorical target classes.
It directly formalizes the group means comparison first introduced back in Bivariate Analysis.
The F-statistic genuinely divides variance between groups by variance within groups.
A genuinely high F-statistic argues for keeping a feature; a genuinely low one argues for dropping it.
ANOVA genuinely relies on roughly normal, similarly spread groups to produce its most reliable results.
Correlation, chi-square, and ANOVA together genuinely complete this module entire filter method family.
